text: nsMsgDBView.Close clears the model keys, flags and levels before notifying both tree adapters about removed rows. It then nulls both tree references and releases database listeners. That preserves the row-count callback contract while ending adapter ownership at close instead of waiting for destruction. The exact cycle and retained UI size remain attributed historical reasoning; no heap/leak test ran. This is not a blanket claim that nulling any reference cures a leak.
title: Closing a database view releases its tree adapters after empty-row notification
